topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening framing, course context, and learning objectives for the lecture series.

topics.label: Biological Foundations and Experimental Modeling of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how cancer originates through accumulated genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation, as well as how tumor cells are cultured and investigated experimentally.

topics.label: Tumor Invasiveness, Stepwise Progression, and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the histological distinction between benign and malignant tumors, detailing the stepwise progression of invasion and the standard nomenclature used to categorize neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the physiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors disrupt normal organ function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Human and Comparative Cancer Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the incidence, prevalence, and mortality patterns of different tumor types across human populations and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Principles and Modalities of Clinical Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical efficacy of early detection and screening strategies across various tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing framing and concluding housekeeping remarks for the lecture.
